target_customer: Energy, insurance, agriculture and logistics firms needing high resolution weather forecasts
problem: Traditional numerical weather prediction is expensive and slow; Silurian sells AI foundation models that forecast weather and can be tailored to customer data.
business_model: API and custom model contracts, enterprise

founders.name: Jayesh K. Gupta
founders.background_notes: Led the first weather foundation model at Microsoft and co-authored Aurora.

competitors.name: Aurora (Microsoft)
competitors.traction_then: Preprint May 2024 reporting better results than GraphCast and IFS-HRES on most targets

competitors.name: GraphCast (Google DeepMind)
competitors.traction_then: Outperformed IFS-HRES on about 90% of 1,380 targets

competitors.name: Pangu-Weather (Huawei)
competitors.traction_then: Released 2023 and sparked wave of AI weather models

technical_complexity.rationale: Training a billion parameter weather model needs research level skill and large compute; the founders built Aurora at Microsoft.

defensibility.rationale: Talent and tuned models help, but Google, Microsoft and ECMWF publish competing open models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Big labs published and productised competing models; Google later released further models per the search results.

market_need_then: Hurricane forecasts and energy and insurance risk are costly; the GFT launch claimed up to 30% better than NOAA and ECMWF on some variables (company claim); partners include Disaster Tech (June 2025) and NOAA AOML.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, 'Solving the Earth's toughest weather problems'

branding.community_and_virality: CEO testified to a House science committee

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a geological period (Silures people) which signals Earth science, but the company's own reason was not found; CEO testimony and GeekWire coverage raised profile.

outcome_analysis: Silurian is an active YC S24 company led by the Microsoft Aurora researcher, launching GFT in 2024 and winning pilots such as Disaster Tech in 2025 and NOAA AOML collaboration. Funding is not verifiable, and Google, Microsoft and ECMWF competitors give it a hard technical race.
notes: Funding unverified: Preqin lists an undisclosed Pioneer Fund seed in September 2024; CB Insights $500K convertible note; StartupHub $6M or $11M; accelerator listing $3M. All conflict, no press release. GeekWire page returned 403 on fetch, cited only from search. Competitor source dates are the paper date, not each model's release. Round added: undisclosed seed from Pioneer Fund in 2024-09 rests on a single database (Preqin); CB Insights lists a 500K convertible note on 2024-09-26 that may be the same money.
